userStories.title: Readable Timeline actors, events and actions
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Display Timeline actors and event/action labels readably and associate its filters with their visible labels.

**Motivation** — R2-3: the Timeline shows the actor as a raw user id, the event as `ticket_event` and the action as a raw code (`TICKET_CREATED`, `status_changed`).

**Approach** — In `pages/[project]/timeline.vue`, load project member names with `useProjectMemberNames(slug)` on mount and render the actor through `nameOf`, falling back to the raw id. Render the event type through `home.activity.eventType.*` (falling back to `humanizeCode`) in the rows and in the filter options, and the action through `humanizeCode` with the raw code as `title`. Associate the Event Type, From and To labels with their controls.

Actor and approver names come from `useProjectMemberNames(slug).nameOf`, which already names the signed-in user when they are not a project member; an id it cannot name renders raw.

Accessible names come from a `<label for>` / control `id` pair where a visible label already sits above the control, and from `aria-label` where the control has no visible label of its own (the per-row notification checkboxes).

Readable labels reuse existing helpers: `codeLabel(t, te, prefix, code)` from `~/lib/fleet-i18n` (translation or the raw code), `humanizeCode(code)` from `~/lib/humanize-code` (words for a code with no key), the `tickets.status.*` keys, the `home.activity.eventType.*` keys and `fleet.command.*` / `fleet.state.*`. Unknown Timeline event types use humanizeCode, not a raw-code-only fallback. Preserve the empty filter option as the existing All translation.

Failure handling: The members read fails on the timeline — Events still render; actors show the raw id; no toast for the members read. Catch the cosmetic members failure independently of loadEvents; load the members exactly once on mount for this slug.

**Scope** — In: Timeline row labels, members-read wiring, Event Type/From/To associations and Jest coverage. Out: Memory filters (US-001), flow display (US-003), ingest labels (US-004), dispatch loading (US-005), SLO date associations (US-006), board/dashboard layout (US-007), changes to the shared member-name resolution rules, and new API routes.

**Interface** — Reuse the existing contracts without changing them:
```ts
// useProjectMemberNames(slug): { members, load, nameOf }
nameOf(userId: string): string | null
humanizeCode(code: string): string
```
The existing member load issues GET /projects/:slug/members with query size: '100'.

**Tests and regression anchors** — Create tests/pages/timeline-readable.spec.ts using mountSfc with the en locale, explicit useProjectMemberNames globals or an alias, and rendered row/option/label attributes. The current harness already lists the member composable among injectable auto-imports; still provide its implementation explicitly. Exercise the real member helper through a request double to prove the one members GET and silent rejection. In tests/pages/timeline.spec.ts, add actor-name, event-type label and action label bindings to createRenderContext; keep the `{{ ... event.eventType ... }}`, `{{ ... event.actorId ... }}` and `{{ ... event.action ... }}` interpolation pins and every other existing assertion as they are. Do not change existing event load/error/empty/pagination behavior.

[unit] When an event's actorId is not a member and not the signed-in user, its actor cell renders that raw actorId.
[unit] When an event has eventType ticket_event, its event cell renders Ticket.
[unit] When an event has eventType foo_event, its event cell renders Foo event.
[unit] When an event has action TICKET_CREATED, it renders Ticket created in an element carrying title="TICKET_CREATED".
[unit] When an event has action status_changed, it renders Status changed.
[unit] The event-type filter option with value ticket_event has the text Ticket.

userStories.title: Readable flow detail titles, dates and job labels
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Make flow detail identify its features and format dates, job codes and pull-request text readably.

**Motivation** — R2-4: the flow detail page is titled "Flow" with the raw flow id as subtitle although the flow's feature names are known; dates print as ISO strings (`2026-11-10T14:07:45.657Z`); stage rows read "Spec review · AGENT · COMPLETED · $0.01"; the pull request line reads "Pull request#36".

**Approach** — Add `flowTitle` to `lib/fleet-flows.ts`. `pages/[project]/flows/[id].vue` uses it as the page title (falling back to `fleet.flows.detail.title`), drops the raw id from the subtitle and shows it as an `ID` row (new key `fleet.flows.detail.id`) in the flow details list, formats Created and Recorded with `timeText`, and renders each row of its own "Flow jobs" list with the command through `codeLabel(t, te, 'fleet.command', command)` and the state through `codeLabel(t, te, 'fleet.state', state)`. `components/fleet/flows/FlowFeatureSection.vue` renders each job row's command through `codeLabel(t, te, 'fleet.command', command)` and its state through `codeLabel(t, te, 'fleet.state', state)`, and renders a space between the Pull request label and `#<number>`. Add `fleet.flows.detail.id` to `en.json` and `zh.json`.

Dates on the flow page are formatted with the existing `timeText(iso)` from `~/lib/fleet-analytics-format` (`new Date(iso).toLocaleString()`, `-` when absent).

Actor and approver names come from `useProjectMemberNames(slug).nameOf`, which already names the signed-in user when they are not a project member; an id it cannot name renders raw. Preserve the page's existing approver-name behavior. Readable labels reuse existing helpers: `codeLabel(t, te, prefix, code)` from `~/lib/fleet-i18n` (translation or the raw code), `humanizeCode(code)` from `~/lib/humanize-code` (words for a code with no key), the `tickets.status.*` keys, the `home.activity.eventType.*` keys and `fleet.command.*` / `fleet.state.*`. Use codeLabel's raw fallback for unknown flow job commands/states.

**Scope** — In: pure flowTitle helper, flow PageHeader/details dates/ID row, both job-list labeling surfaces, explicit pull-request whitespace, both locales and Jest tests. Out: Memory labels (US-001), Timeline member loading (US-002), ingest project display (US-004), dispatch/job options loading (US-005), other accessible names/contrast (US-006), board/dashboard layout (US-007), and any flow polling, answer/stop gating, grouping or wire-contract changes.

**Interface** — New exported helper, verbatim signature and algorithm:
```ts
flowTitle(flow: { features: readonly { feature: string }[] }): string | null
```
The feature names joined with `", "`, or `null` when there are none. Existing helper contract:
```ts
codeLabel(t, te, prefix: string, code: string): string
```

**Tests and regression anchors** — Create tests/lib/fleet-flows-title.spec.ts and tests/pages/flow-detail-readable.spec.ts, mounting both the real page and FlowFeatureSection with real en labels. Use mountSfc and capture PageHeader props as well as rendered rows. Add `te: () => false` to the useI18n stub in tests/components/flow-feature-section.spec.ts so labels fall back to the raw code; every existing assertion stays as it is. Add `te: () => false` to tests/pages/fleet-flow-detail.spec.ts. Its AC-10 test asserts the raw ISO string `2026-01-02T03:04:05.000Z` for Created, which this story replaces with `timeText`; change that one expectation to the value of `new Date('2026-01-02T03:04:05.000Z').toLocaleString()`. Every other existing assertion stays as it is (with `te` false, the flow jobs row still reads `RUN · RUN · QUEUED · $0.50`). Keep untrusted strings interpolation-only and retain existing overview-failure/polling behavior.

userStories.title: Readable and contained admin ingest table
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Resolve ingest project labels and job links from an existing project-list read and contain the table's screen-reader-only header within its scroll wrapper.

**Motivation** — R2-5: the admin fleet analytics bundle-ingest table shows raw job and project ids; at 390 px the page scrolls sideways by about 30 px because the table header's screen-reader-only text escapes its scroll box.

**Approach** — Add the `IngestProject` type, the `projects()` method on `useFleetAnalyticsAdmin()` and the `projects` prop to `FleetAnalyticsIngestTable`. The project cell shows the project name when the id is in `projects`, else the raw id. The job cell shows the short job id (full id as `title`) plus `#<leaseEpoch>`, linked to `/<slug>/fleet/jobs/<jobId>` when the project is known. The element that wraps the table carries `relative` with `overflow-x-auto`. `pages/admin/fleet/analytics.vue` calls `projects()` once on mount and passes the result as `projects`, using `[]` when the read fails.

The project list for the ingest table is read through a new `projects()` method on `useFleetAnalyticsAdmin()`, not by the page directly (`.nax/rules/web.md`: API calls live in composables).

A shortened id is the first 8 characters of the id. The full raw value stays available as the element's `title`.

jsdom has no layout engine, so layout and touch-target fixes are asserted through the Tailwind classes the rendered element carries. The audit verified the live effect.

Failure handling: `useFleetAnalyticsAdmin().projects()` rejects on `/admin/fleet/analytics` — The ingest table renders with `projects = []` (raw project ids, no job links); no toast. This cosmetic request is separate from refreshAll, range/visibility refreshes and existing ingest/spend error handling. Do not introduce a timer, extra project refreshes, or changes to admin access enforcement.

**Scope** — In: display projection type, additive composable method, backward-compatible table prop, shortened ids/conditional links, positioned scroll wrapper, one page-level cosmetic lookup and Jest coverage. Out: Memory/Timeline/flow labels (US-001 to US-003), dispatch loading (US-005), home chip contrast (US-006), board/dashboard layout (US-007), new endpoints, API/OpenAPI changes, and unrelated analytics calculations or rerun behavior.

**Interface** — Target contracts:
```ts
// Exported from apps/web/lib/fleet-analytics-types.ts
export interface IngestProject { id: string; slug: string; name: string }
// FleetAnalyticsIngestTable; projects defaults to []
defineProps<{ rows: readonly IngestRowDto[]; busyJobId: string | null; projects?: readonly IngestProject[] }>()
// Additional method returned by useFleetAnalyticsAdmin()
projects: () => Promise<IngestProject[]>
```
`projects: () => Promise<IngestProject[]>`, which issues `GET /projects` and maps each row to `{ id, slug, name }`. Keep the pre-existing spend, ingest reads and re-run calls unchanged.

**Tests and regression anchors** — Create tests/components/fleet-ingest-projects.spec.ts; extend tests/composables/useFleetAnalytics.spec.ts for the projected request result and tests/pages/admin-fleet-analytics.spec.ts for successful/failed prop wiring and the silent fallback. Use mountSfc and rendered DOM/props, retaining chart stubs. In tests/pages/admin-fleet-analytics.spec.ts, make makeGet answer the projects route with an empty array; every existing assertion stays as it is. Existing tests/components/fleet-ingest-table.spec.ts retain their behavior with the optional prop omitted. Assert relative and overflow-x-auto on the actual table wrapper, not a source substring or a non-layout renderer's measured width.

userStories.title: Truthful permission and dispatch-option loading
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Distinguish unknown permissions and unresolved option names from actual denial or final raw-id fallback on dispatch/job detail pages. **Motivation** — R2-1: `/[project]/fleet/dispatch` renders "You do not have permission to dispatch jobs" while the project permissions are still loading, then replaces it with the form. A permitted user is first told they are refused. R1-15: the fleet job page shows the raw repo id and runner id until the repo/runner options load. **Approach** — `pages/[project]/fleet/dispatch.vue` renders `LoadingState` while the project permissions are pending and only shows `dispatch-no-permission` once they have loaded without `fleet.job.dispatch`; the existing `

` element and its `canDispatch` computed line unchanged (`tests/pages/fleet-dispatch-page.spec.ts` pins both); the loading state is added around it: a `LoadingState` when project permissions are pending, and the existing chain otherwise. A value that is still loading renders the existing `common.loading` text (en `Loading...`), never a hardcoded character. Failure handling: `useFleetDispatchOptions().load()` rejects on the fleet job page — `settled` becomes `true`; the subtitle and Runner field fall back to the raw id. Preserve the existing rejection propagation and the job page's silent options-read catch; do not leave the loading text on screen indefinitely. Keep settled true after the first terminal outcome, including during subsequent loads. **Scope** — In: outer permission-pending presentation, additive options settlement state, repo/assigned-runner loading text, final failure fallbacks, and Jest fixtures/behavior tests. Out: Memory/Timeline/flow/ingest display (US-001 to US-004), notification/SLO labeling and contrast (US-006), chip/board/dashboard sizing (US-007), changes to permission evaluation, role-name gating, backend authorization, and Round 1 R1-16 (job page detail grid layout); it needs a layout decision. **Interface** — Existing read-only integration: ```ts useProjectPermissions(slug): Permissions // Permissions carries permissions: ComputedRef and pending: Ref ``` Target for `useFleetDispatchOptions(slug)`: also returns `settled: Ref`, `false` until the first `load()` call resolves or rejects, then `true`. `repoName` / `runnerName` keep their current fallback to the raw id. Keep all current returned members: repos, runners, moreRepos, moreRunners, load, profileOptions, labelOptions, repoName, runnerName. Preserve this exact gate: ```ts const canDispatch = computed(() => permissions.value.has('fleet.job.dispatch')) ``` **Tests and regression anchors** — Use three-session-tdd because permission gating is involved: the test-writer creates failing behavioral tests and updates affected test fixtures without source changes; implementation preserves test files. Create tests/pages/fleet-dispatch-loading.spec.ts using mountSfc and pending permission refs. Extend tests/composables/useFleetDispatchOptions.spec.ts to cover initial/resolved/rejected settled state and fallback, and mount the job page to inspect PageHeader subtitle and fleet-job-runner. In tests/pages/fleet-job-detail.spec.ts, fleet-job-detail-workflow.spec.ts, fleet-job-agent-result.spec.ts and fleet-job-fix-action.spec.ts, add `settled: ref(true)` to each useFleetDispatchOptions double; every existing assertion stays as it is. In fleet-job-budget-gates.spec.ts add the same field to its job-page options double; every existing assertion stays as it is. Read permission-nav.ts and existing permission gate mounts for fixture patterns; update additional affected doubles additively if necessary, without weakening guards or assertions. The additive field must not change shared options behavior on schedules, budgets, threads, repo config or the jobs list.

userStories.title: Accessible notification and SLO controls with contrast-safe attention
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Name the remaining audited email/date controls and restore the dashboard attention chip's contrast using an existing safe surface.

**Motivation** — R2-6: axe reports form controls with no accessible name: the email and in-app checkboxes on `/settings/notifications`, the From/To date inputs on `/admin/slos` and `/[project]/timeline`, the event-type select on the timeline, and the kind/status selects on the Memory page. R2-7: on the light dashboard the "N need attention" chip is 4.21:1, under WCAG AA.

**Approach** — `pages/settings/notifications.vue` gives each row's email checkbox the `aria-label` from new key `notifications.preferences.emailFor` (takes `{category}`, the row's translated label). `pages/admin/slos.vue` associates its From and To labels with the date inputs. `components/home/HomeProjectList.vue` renders the attention chip on `bg-card`. Add the key to `en.json` (`Email: {category}`) and `zh.json`.

Only the email checkboxes on `/settings/notifications` get an `aria-label`: each in-app checkbox is already named by its row's `<label for>`.

Accessible names come from a `<label for>` / control `id` pair where a visible label already sits above the control, and from `aria-label` where the control has no visible label of its own (the per-row notification checkboxes).

The "need attention" chip keeps its red text and border but drops the `bg-destructive/10` tint, sitting on `bg-card`; `--status-rejected` on `--card` is already pinned at 4.5:1 or more by `tests/lib/token-contrast.spec.ts`.

Test harness: page and component ACs mount with `mountSfc` (`apps/web/tests/helpers/mount-sfc.ts`) and assert on the rendered DOM, as `tests/pages/notification-settings-page.spec.ts` does; the binding-only harness of `tests/pages/admin-slos-mount.spec.ts` cannot observe `id` / `for` attributes.

**Scope** — In: category email aria-labels, both locale entries, the SLO date for/id pairs, the HomeProjectList chip surface and Jest coverage. userStories.title: Board action hierarchy and compact responsive layouts
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Restore board primary-action hierarchy, align column/dashboard cards and enlarge audited phone-width filter targets.

**Motivation** — R1-17: the project board shows "New Ticket" and "Import Issue" as two filled primary buttons. R1-18: the board's Created column header is taller than the others (its inline New Ticket button). R1-19: empty "My tickets" / "Approvals" dashboard cards stretch to the tallest card in the row. R1-20: at phone width the fleet jobs state chips and the board priority chips are under 44 px tall.

**Approach** — On `pages/[project]/index.vue` the Import Issue button uses `variant="outline"`; the priority filter chips carry `h-11 sm:h-9`. In `components/TicketBoard.vue` every column header row carries `data-testid="board-column-header-<STATUS>"` and `h-8`, and the inline New Ticket button carries `h-7`. `components/home/HomeNeedsYou.vue`'s card grid carries `items-start`. On `pages/[project]/fleet/index.vue` each state filter chip carries `h-11 sm:h-8`.

Touch-target fixes set `h-11` below the `sm` breakpoint and an explicit height from `sm` up: `sm:h-9` for the board priority chips (their current height) and `sm:h-8` for the fleet state chips. The fleet chips have no explicit height today (about 26 px from `py-1 text-xs`), so on desktop they grow to 32 px; this is intended.

`TicketBoard` column header rows get `data-testid="board-column-header-<STATUS>"` so tests can find them.

jsdom has no layout engine, so layout and touch-target fixes are asserted through the Tailwind classes the rendered element carries. The audit verified the live effect.

**Scope** — In: the four named board/dashboard/fleet layout surfaces, header testids and Jest behavioral class/prop coverage. Out: Memory/Timeline/flow/ingest labels (US-001 to US-004), dispatch loading (US-005), attention-chip contrast and other accessible names (US-006), changing filters or ticket business rules, and Round 1 R1-16 (job page detail grid layout); it needs a layout decision. Do not expand this into filter select height or breadcrumb/other small-target fixes deferred by the feature.

**Interface** — No new exported function or API contract. Header markers are `board-column-header-CREATED`, `board-column-header-VERIFIED`, `board-column-header-IN_PROGRESS`, `board-column-header-VERIFY_FIX`, `board-column-header-CLOSED` and `board-column-header-REJECTED`; preserve existing board-column-<STATUS> ids and create/open-ticket events. New Ticket remains the default primary action. Keep literal Tailwind classes in Vue templates and retain shared ticket-chip token helpers.

**Tests and regression anchors** — Create tests/components/board-layout.spec.ts with mountSfc coverage of rendered header/button/grid classes and the relevant page chips. Use tests/pages/project-board.spec.ts, tests/pages/fleet-jobs-list.spec.ts and tests/components/home-needs-you.spec.ts as neighboring examples; no existing spec pins the button variant, header height, grid alignment or chip height this story changes, so existing assertions remain unchanged. Assert the default variant on New Ticket and outline on Import Issue through component props, all six h-8 header rows through the new testids, and responsive class pairs on each actual filter chip. Preserve the existing home.needsYouEmpty branch when all three totals are zero and its arrays are empty; the items-start change applies only to the nonempty card grid. Do not infer physical heights from the custom renderer or introduce new e2e specs. Read the existing redesign master plan before these additive layout edits.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] When pages/[project]/index.vue is mounted, the Import Issue Button has variant outline.
[unit] On that page, the New Ticket Button keeps the default variant.
[unit] On that page, each priority filter chip carries the classes h-11 and sm:h-9.
[unit] When TicketBoard is mounted with tickets in every status, it renders six board-column-header-<STATUS> elements, each carrying the class h-8.
[unit] The Created column's New Ticket button in TicketBoard carries the class h-7.
[unit] When HomeNeedsYou is mounted with items to show, its card grid carries the class items-start.
[unit] When pages/[project]/fleet/index.vue is mounted, each state filter chip carries the classes h-11 and sm:h-8.
[unit] When HomeNeedsYou is mounted with empty tickets, approvals and jobs arrays and all three totals equal to zero, it still renders the existing home.needsYouEmpty text instead of the card grid.

routing.reasoning: Four tightly bounded presentation surfaces use ordinary variants and Tailwind utilities; there is no new abstraction, state model or business logic.

analysis: Repository and architecture: This is an enhancement to the existing Bun/Turborepo web workspace, not greenfield work. The execution root is /Users/williamkhoo/workspace/subrina-coder/projects/koda/repos/koda. No codebase-memory MCP tools are exposed in this session, so graph-first discovery was unavailable; direct Read/Grep/Glob exploration was used instead. Contrary to the detected Codebase Context table, apps/web is Nuxt 4 SSR with Vue 3, not Next.js: apps/web/package.json:6 builds with nuxt, apps/web/package.json:33 declares nuxt ^4.6.4, and .nax/mono/apps/web/context.md:22 identifies the stack. Preserve the existing root-level pages/components/composables structure. .nax/rules/web.md:22 requires useApi-based requests inside composables/utilities; the web has no generated API client. This feature needs no API, Prisma, OpenAPI, generated-client, dependency, or persistent-data migration. The new project lookup is an existing GET /projects request, not a new contract. All seven stories are independent and have workdir apps/web and dependencies []; no exported-symbol seam crosses stories. Locale changes by US-001, US-003 and US-006 share en.json/zh.json and must be merged additively without overwriting another story's keys. No production code was changed or tests executed while drafting this PRD. US-001 findings and impact: apps/web/pages/[project]/memory.vue:13 currently destructures only t; its filter labels/selects at :132-148 have no for/id associations, the subject cell at :186 prints item.subject raw, the non-NOTE object branch at :196 prints item.object raw, and the kind badge at :198 prints item.kind raw. apps/web/composables/useMemory.ts:19 defines MemoryItem with string subject/predicate/object/kind/status: this is display-only work and does not require changing its query, retirement, debounce, pagination or permission behavior. Add lib/memory-subject.ts and use it from the page; link ticket ids directly through the existing CUID-capable ticket route, not via an additional lookup. Only ticket:/agent: with a nonempty suffix are recognized, splitting at the first colon. Prefix-free or empty-prefixed subjects stay unchanged. The short form is the first eight characters of the extracted id and the raw subject is retained as title. Translate status objects only for predicate status when tickets.status.
